items.text: B's title adds the hero tagline to the brand name. A's title is the brand name alone.
items.evidence: A title: "AEP Texas"; B title: "AEP Texas | Knowledge Is Power"

items.text: B has a meta description and a charset meta. A has none of these but does have google-site-verification, cache-control and pragma metas.
items.evidence: A meta_names: google-site-verification, cache-control, pragma, viewport; B: charset, viewport, description

items.text: B uses semantic landmark elements (header, main, section, aside). A has only nav and footer.
items.evidence: A semantic: header 0, main 0, section 0, aside 0; B: header 1, main 1, section 3, aside 1

items.text: Heading levels for the feature blocks differ. A tags Meter/Outages/Community as h3, while B promotes them to h2 and makes the three promo cards h3.
items.evidence: A outline: h3 'View Your Meter Order Status'; B outline: h2 'View Your Meter Order Status', h3 'GET REVVED UP FOR ELECTRIC CARS'

items.evidence: B outline includes h2 'Enroll in outage alerts'; A outline lacks it although A_slice_01 shows the text

items.text: A uses one custom typeface for all text. B uses a system font stack.

items.text: B's H2 is larger than A's.
items.evidence: h2 font_size: A 32px, B 36.8px

features.statement: Page title combines the brand name with a tagline, separated by a pipe.
Head includes a charset meta and a descriptive meta description, with little other verification or cache metadata.
Uses semantic landmark elements (header, main, section, aside) to structure the page.
Heading hierarchy is clean: feature blocks are h2 and sub-cards h3, with section titles included in the outline.
Text uses a generic system font stack (Helvetica Neue/Arial) rather than a custom web font.
Section headings (h2) are large, around 37px.
Top navigation labels are title case, small, and grouped beside the logo.
Header is compact with a small logo, and the nav sits beside the logo.
Content sits in a narrower centered container with wide side gutters.
Hero subcopy sits in a translucent white box with an accent-colored left border.
Quick-link strip is a solid accent-red bar with small white text labels and no icons.
A section uses a warm off-white or beige background band to separate it from white areas.
Tip or promo is a white card with an accent top border, shadow, and underlined text link with arrow.
Primary CTAs are solid red buttons with bold white text.
Secondary CTA is an outlined red button, so CTA treatments vary between solid and outline.
Promos appear as equal-sized bordered cards with image on top and red uppercase titles below.
Alert-signup strip is a solid mid-gray band with white text and a white button with red text.
Feature items are laid out as alternating full-width image/text rows in a zig-zag.
Feature images have slightly rounded corners.
Footer is dark charcoal with light gray links and a large bold white phone number on the right.
Body text is a near-black charcoal color.
Layout uses CSS grid with comparatively few flex containers.
Icons are text glyphs (☰ menu, → arrow) instead of image or sprite icons; language link is plain text.
Images are cropped to uniform small sizes, with all images carrying descriptive alt text.
DOM is compact, with few nodes, shallow nesting, few classes, inline styles and ARIA attributes.
Page is self-contained with one inline style block, a single script, and no external stylesheets.
Login is a single native dialog element containing a form.
Few CSS transitions are defined, so interaction animation is minimal.
